byu-har.name: Byu Har (Min Oat Myanmar)
byu-har.note: SAFETY: INCARCERATED. Described by BBC as one of Myanmar's biggest hip-hop artists; son of songwriter Naing Myanmar. Arrested 24 May 2023 after a Facebook Live criticising power cuts and calling Min Aung Hlaing incompetent, held at North Dagon Police Station, and sentenced to 20 years on 24 Aug 2023. Press reports charge incitement (Penal Code art. 505(a)) and treason, but AP quotes a relative saying it was unclear which he was convicted of - so no single offence is asserted here. Rappler (Mar 2025) documents pro-military Telegram doxing that preceded the arrest. Stage name only; do not add family details beyond published press, and do not attempt to identify him.

disputes.statusNote: settled as to arrest and sentence
disputes.claim: On 23 May 2023 Byu Har posted a four-minute Facebook video from his home in Yangon's North Dagon Township criticising four-hours-on/four-hours-off loadshedding, calling the electricity minister 'a fool' and Min Aung Hlaing 'a stupid incompetent fool', comparing the junta period unfavourably to Aung San Suu Kyi's, and stating his home address in the caption, inviting arrest. Arrested by soldiers and police that night; held at North Dagon Police Station, then Insein. Charged under Penal Code s.505(a); the junta's statement cited incitement to disrupt peace and stability and spreading propaganda. Sentenced to 20 years on 23 August 2023 - reported as the harshest celebrity sentence of the crackdown.
disputes.response: Byu Har made no public response after arrest. The junta's framing is the response on record.
disputes.corroboration: STRONG - five or more independent outlets: AP, BBC, RFA, Mizzima, The Irrawaddy, Bangkok Post, VOA, PEN America, plus Rappler's investigation of the doxing infrastructure. Rappler documents 32 arrests in Jan-May 2023 from Ka Ka Han posts alone, and a FOEIM school data leak exposing hundreds of students' details.
disputes.safety: SEVERE. Living prisoner, 20-year sentence. Do not publish his home address, family details, or the specific Telegram channel handles - the doxing mechanism is the documented cause of the arrest. UN Special Rapporteurs called out Telegram's moderation failure in Myanmar in March 2023.

relations.note: NOT a member. Recorded to make explicit that a major post-coup rapper is absent from RAJ, and to carry his incarceration status. No source places him in the collective.

hein-htet-zaw.name: Hein Htet Zaw
hein-htet-zaw.note: THREE NAMES, ONE PERSON. 'HOT' and 'OT the Croc' are both this artist - two independent publisher descriptions state the identity (Chartmetric's bio string-concatenates 'This is Hein Htet Zaw (a.k.a) HOT.' with 'OT the croc, born Mandalay', and the Burmese Plug Talk podcast episode description reads 'Ot the croc aka Hein Htet Zaw'). The release titles HOT BLODDED CROC and CROC MOVE (SEASON 1) corroborate the croc motif on the HOT streaming identity. Born Mandalay, grew up on the north side of the city. Rapping from 2013; producing beats from 2016, and described as 'one of the most productive beat producers from Area 952' - Area 952 is UNVERIFIED as to what it denotes. Credited as (WCC) in Jan 2014, so affiliated with that crew by then; 'Studio Mandalay' is credited on the same track. Collaborators he names: Frezzy, A Tee, Datty Dax, L.O.D, BIGG, Weei4, S-Two, Tyrant, Jerryx, JCZ, Bobby Beatz. CAUTION: do not conflate with Hein Htet (rock band Out Of The Rule) or Hein Htet Aung - three distinct Burmese artists. Do NOT record ဦးတိုက် as his script name: ဦး is the honorific 'U', making ဦးတိုက် read as 'U Toik', which is not a plausible mononym and not a transliteration of 'OT'. No source uses it.

Most have no entity record; their ids here are placeholders pending act-level sourcing, and no solo discography exists for any of them. 'Channel Wildboy' appears on the Nov 2012 MDY All Stars compilation, which independently confirms Wildboy membership for Channel. A Mandalay base is INFERRED from Oasix and Y-Zet, not stated on the mixtape page itself.

vip.name: VIP (Rock$tar)
vip.status: active; Ah Boy is a former member
vip.note: ONE GROUP, TWO NAMES - not a name collision. A 2009 Myanmar Hip Hop Channel interview has Kyaw Htut Swe stating the group began in 2007 with Ah Boy and Htein Win, that Htein Win is Kyaw Htut Swe's younger brother, and that for various reasons only three stayed long-term, with Jouk Jack added. The 2009 mixtape 'Titans (G-Fam, BNW, Fire-Cracker, Rockstar)' places Rock$tar alongside three OTHER crews, and the collective track 'Revison (Rock Star)' credits all four members. Wikipedia renders the name as 'VIP (Rock$tar)'. Htein Win is not given his own artist record, so the four-member group appears as three member ids. Kyaw Htut Swe also states candidly that the members joined for the sample CDs, not for musical ability. Ah Boy's exit is the documented event: his Wikipedia article lists him as 'Formerly of Rock$tar' and 'former lead vocalist', and a Feb 2013 Burmese headline implies a grievance about him not pulling his weight rather than a rupture. No response from the group is on record.

Members: Ye' Myat, Na Yem, Na Jyam, Nga Ye', Aung Phyo, Kyaw Zin, Yan Naing, Doe-Z, Thiri Yadanar, Su Thet Nge, plus special guest No No. Recorded at studio TKG with lyrics and beats by MRC. Names recorded here but without their own entity record: Na Yem, Na Jyam, Nga Ye', Kyaw Zin, Yan Naing, Doe-Z, Thiri Yadanar, Su Thet Nge, No No.

thar-nge-mcfamily.name: Thar Nge (MC Family)
thar-nge-mcfamily.note: The strongest Mandalay-scene evidence in the fan archive: two of Oasix's and Y-Zet's seven guest appearances on the 2013 mixtape, from the crew they both belonged to at the time. Members and associates: Joe Joe, B-Boi, Khaing Soe, Timmy, Wailin Phyo, Thaw Thaw, and Chan Myae (Mandalay Rapperz Crew). CITY UNVERIFIED - no source states Mandalay, though the crossover with both Wildboy members makes it plausible. CAUTION: at least three distinct Burmese artists are called Thar Nge - this rap crew, the Myanmar Idol S2 winner Thar Nge (b. Zaw Win Htun 1992, pop/R&B), and jazz vocalist Thar Nge IV (b. 1988, Yangon). Never merge. Also distinct from Thar Thar, Htet Yan's duet partner.

schema.title: Myanmar Hip-Hop Open Data Archive
schema.description: Knowledge-graph style schema. All facts must carry at least one source ID and a confidence level.

fields.name: string
fields.city: string|null (origin or base; use base for diaspora acts)
fields.base: string|null (current base, e.g. 'Munich, Germany' for diaspora acts)
fields.realName: string|null (only when published by a cited source)
fields.genre: string[] (e.g. trap, drill, boom-bap, jersey club; only when sourced, never from a single platform genre field)

fields.name: string
fields.kind: crew | association | collective | label | studio | media

fields.title: string
fields.artistId: string (or artistIdA/artistIdB for a duo/collab billing)
fields.year: int|null (null when only a range or a re-release date is known)
fields.yearNote: string|null (explains a null or uncertain year)
fields.type: album | EP | single | mixtape | compilation | live | collection
encyclopedia | article | interview | podcast | video | database | magazine | journal | advocacy | music | website | archive | aggregator
fields.title: string
fields.author: string|absent
fields.archivedUrl: string|null (use when the live URL is dead)
fields.quality: primary | high | medium-high | medium | low | secondary | unverified

fields.label: string
fields.artistNames: string[] (named in the sources but not yet promoted to Artist records)
fields.confidence: string (free text; may qualify per claim)

fields.path: string (served by the consuming app, e.g. /media/...)

fields.type: diss track | crew exit | legal/censorship | legal/political | legal/other | credit dispute
fields.parties: artist or crew id[] (only where an entity record exists)
fields.partyNames: string[] (named in the sources but without an entity record)
fields.targetDescription: string|null (prose, NOT an id - the target is often the state or an unnamed person)
fields.period: string (free text: year, range, or 'documented 2016, ongoing')
fields.claim: string (what is alleged or what happened, always attributed)
fields.corroboration: string (must name whether the support is single-source)

fields.type: member_of | released | performed_at | pioneer_of | associated_with | mentioned_in | documented_in | signed_to | founded | featured_on | dissed | produced_for | part_of

rules: Every claim must reference at least one source ID.
No copyrighted text is stored - only factual metadata (names, dates, places).
Image records hold credits and source links only; binaries are not redistributed by this repository.
Image.alt and Image.credit are defaults. A Period may override both, because one image file is captioned differently in different periods.
Period.artistNames holds acts that the cited sources name but that have no Artist record yet. They are deliberately not promoted until an act-level source supports one.

A Dispute is a CLAIM by at least one party, often disputed by the other. Never state an allegation as established fact: record who claimed it, what the claim is, and whether it is corroborated. `corroboration` must say 'single-source' where that is the case.

Dispute.status distinguishes settled (documented) from disputed (two incompatible accounts) from unresolved (evidence is thin or the primary source is dead) from structurally unresolved (the mechanism itself is the finding, e.g. an absent legal category).

Do not create a causal link between two events merely because sources place them adjacently. The Y-Zet concert death of 2017 and the 'Shwee Die' diss of 2011 are six years apart and the fatal fight began with accidental contact while dancing.

In this scene 'beef' is usually a genre label or a song title, not a documented grievance. Multi-artist posse cuts titled with the word 'beef' are not feuds. Only code a Dispute where a claim, a target and some evidence exist.
Where a dispute targets a living person who is deliberately unnamed in the work itself, keep them unnamed. A veiled diss stays veiled.
Conflicts are flagged as CONFLICTED and resolved by human review, never by AI.
Burmese script names are preserved in the aliases field.

identityStatus is mandatory whenever realName is null. Use 'pseudonym' or 'anonymised' for post-coup acts whose legal identity is deliberately withheld. Never infer a real name from a pseudonym, a producer credit, or a shared surname.
Never attribute a real name to someone at risk. A stage name published in press stays a stage name.
Release.year may be null when only a re-release date or an uncertain range is known; explain it in yearNote. Do not silently convert a platform date into a release year.
Suspected re-releases are flagged in Release.note rather than presented as a second, earlier release.
Conflicting counts or dates are preserved with both values and their sources. Do not harmonise a disagreement the sources have not resolved.
Genre is recorded only when a cited source states it. A single streaming platform's genre field is metadata, not a stylistic claim; it is not sufficient on its own.

Third-party AI music-analytics aggregators (musicmetricsvault, sounddrain, viberate) publish fabricated prose and invented statistics. Never cite them. Platform metadata may be cited only from the platform itself.
When a source is offline, cite it via archivedUrl (web.archive.org). A dead URL is not a reason to drop a well-evidenced fact.
Platform artist pages are ambiguous for generic names. Record the platform's numeric artist id on the Source so a future checker can disambiguate collisions.
